_note: Human-owned prose sidecar for the build journal (YED-119). Keyed by build date (YYYY-MM-DD). Each entry: a short headline + a summary of no more than 3 lines answering WHAT was done, WHY, and the VALUE — no fluff. The generator (build_journal.py) merges these over the auto-derived facts (PRs, Linear refs, rigor telemetry). Leave a date out and the entry still renders from facts alone. This is the deliberate low-fluff seed to be revisited later with a fuller voice.

2026-09-13.headline: The write path that can't be skipped — and the judge that caught the switch
2026-09-13.summary: Roadmap v2's Phase-0 gate shipped (#73): ADR-9 draws the PII boundary in three tiers — Notion may hold contact detail only when Alex supplied it, the Supabase spine holds professional-public identity and never an email or phone, the hub carries aggregates and public figures — and one module, `spine_client.py`, becomes the only way anything writes to the graph. It hard-fails: per-table allowlists, a recursive email/phone scan through metadata JSON, a denylist backstop for inbox rows, and a rule that any column may be nulled but only known ones set — which is how the one stored email was removed through the guard itself. Six copy-pasted writers folded into it; the hub got `npm run check` as its own failing guard (#16).  — Second ship: the first cross-provider judge split worth having. Gemini scored the guard 1.0 across the board; Sonnet flagged it at 0.68 because `req()` shipped with a public `guard_writes=False` — a disable switch on a hard-fail guard, contradicting the docstring's own "no in-run override." Sonnet was right; the switch is gone, the writer scan now catches JS `fetch` and the doc-KB tables, and three regression tests pin all of it. The value: a leak-prevention property the code can prove, and a calibration record that shows which judge to trust.

2026-09-12.headline: Back to one source of truth — and the rules so it stays that way
2026-09-12.summary: Four parallel worktrees converged to main in a single day (#60–#64): the document knowledge base shipped Phase A plus A.5 retrieval hardening and the first two Phase-B stories (YED-118/156/157), the Inbox Intelligence Miner landed as a first-class market-intelligence signal source with its own ADR (YED-153), the OBS capture lane replaced the dead Granola path (YED-154), and the job-search content rulings plus a roadmap reconcile cleared a five-item decision backlog. Convergence worked on its own; what didn't was everything around it.  — Second ship: the build-quality judge caught ADR-8 Increment 1 claiming a scope it had not held — a quorum split, Gemini 1.0 against Sonnet 0.55 — and the flagging seat was right. The system graph was persisting edge types nothing read, a direct violation of the ADR's own rule, and one git subprocess per artifact had put the rebuild at ~5s against a stated <2s. Fixed by deletion (0.2s, roughly 25× faster), the false "scope held" claim struck in place rather than quietly rewritten, and a --selftest added so the extractor cannot regress silently (#65). A decision record that shows its own wrong claim is worth more than one that hides it.  — Third ship: the reconciliation itself. The chaos was never branches — code had self-merged unprompted — it was sessions: three Claude sessions shared the main checkout while it sat on a feature branch, each believing another one owned it, and Linear carried six shipped issues still marked Backlog. Converged from a scratch worktree with server-side PRs (the charter's quiesce-first rule could not be met, so the method routed around it), corrected Linear to git truth, retired a four-month-stale priorities block, wrote the git conventions into CLAUDE.md and the reconciliation charter into the repo, rescued five machine-local plan files that two ADRs still cited, and sharded the telemetry ledger per session so the one file every worktree appended to can never conflict again (#67, #68; YED-159). Still open: the denylist review that gates the whole-inbox scan, and ADR-7's acceptance sits in review (#69). Diagnosing it wasn't abstract — one of those sessions hit the failure live: it stashed a sibling session's uncommitted work, watched a branch tip move three times between two commands, and found the main checkout sitting on another session's feature branch. The rules got written straight off that wreckage. The value: a repo where "what's open" and "what shipped" finally agree, and the failure mode written down before it recurs.  — Fourth entry, the pipeline in use rather than under construction: /check-new-events ran against the coming week and found nine events on the calendar, none carrying a PIPELINE block, so the raw-calendar fallback did the intake — Luma, Meetup and the Gmail registration receipts resolved what the invites truncated (the Notion-hosted "Context is King" webinar, Miracle Software's middleware pitch, the seven names on the LeadDev agenda, Ryan Booz of pganalyze). Dedup against Notion came back empty, the Deep Read ledger was clean, the renderer was registered: a clean start, and one calendar defect caught before it cost a missed session (the Goldcast receipt says 1pm ET; the invite said 9am).  — Fifth entry, the run stopping exactly where it is designed to: nine full briefs do not fit one session — each research fan-out spends roughly 40–70 of a ~200-search cap — so the pipeline surfaced a tiering call (four in-person rooms plus the RevGenius system-of-action panel now, two vendor livestreams next session, two webinars roundup-only) and held at the Step 5 gate with the steering intake batched into the same reply. Nothing was written to Notion. Still open: the go on the tier split. The value: the human-in-the-loop design holding under a real week's load, and a hard constraint doing the prioritization the calendar never does.  — Sixth entry, what the flagged build actually is: ADR-8 Increment 1 is a derived graph over the repo's own build artifacts — every skill, command, hook, ADR and the references between them — rebuilt by a stdlib-only extractor on SessionStart and Stop hooks. The point was never the graph; it was that the rigor layer had been good at recording and bad at watching, because every control was invoked (a command someone types) rather than triggered. Proof it flipped: an ordinary `git mv` on a referenced file surfaced a finding at the next session start naming all three citing sites, with nobody invoking anything. It also turned up two defects in `check-refs.sh` — the tool it generalizes, and the one feeding the judge's completeness cap: first that path templates like `evolution-log-{slug}.md` were being reported as missing files, so the cap had been firing on artifacts whose references were never broken; then that the fix over-corrected and began swallowing real broken references sharing a line with a template, which is a reference checker hiding references. Both are pinned now by the extractor's self-test, whose second assertion checks the two tools still agree — the ADR says their rules are shared verbatim, and until now that was enforced by a comment reading "change both", which cannot enforce itself. The value: the check that guards every other build finally has a check of its own (#61, #65).

2026-09-11.headline: Rulings that had been blocking a workstream, and a rubric that stopped discriminating
2026-09-11.summary: Cleared the five-item content-quality decision backlog that had left the invariants contract paused since spring: variants at 3, visual briefs mandatory, stance advisory rather than an enforced gate, and ADR-6 settling the research brief as a discrete Content Draft with the Event page carrying only the head — the dual-write was the real smell, and discrete wins because Content Drafts carry multi-Event relations, Goal/Outcome properties and clean RAG provenance that page-body text cannot. Out of it came an archetype upgrade rather than just a ruling: the two per-event posts are now one deliberate arc — pre-event table-sets macro (the topic's current state, trends, recent developments), then micro (the perspective the event description and the presenter carry), then the implications in broader context; post-event cashes that setup against what was actually said, agreed and argued, mining the brief's Pre→Post Gap. Stance-license rose low-medium to medium once it was clear the May rule predated Field Guide v2's research depth. Role-radar took v2.4 the same day — A-tier threshold 78 to 85, because at ≥78 half of everything scanned landed in A: the registry is pre-filtered to AI-native PLG companies, so roles clear 75–80 on mechanism, tier and leverage before location is even counted. Alongside, the knowledge base took its A.5 retrieval hardening (eval set v2, vendored metrics, a local reranker, a 3-arm harness) and the judge gained cross-provider evidence parity. The value: content rules that are decided and wired rather than re-debated, and a scoring tier that means something again.

2026-09-09.headline: A voice rule earned from a real correction
2026-09-09.summary: Codified the TABLE-SET rule into the content voice system (style guide v0.9): every event post must plainly say what this is / that it was a webinar-panel-briefing / who presented BEFORE the why and the value — context → why → value — with a matching anti-pattern row. It came from a live correction on the shipped GLM-5.3 post: the Variant C draft dove straight into the insight and lost the table-setting, so the fix hardens the lesson into the standing pipeline rather than re-catching it by hand each time. Shipped the GLM-5.3 frontier-crossing carousel (HTML → rendered 4:5 PDF) as the visual companion, and marked the YED-130 graph consolidation done in the roadmap. The value: the recurring "diving straight in" failure is now a rule the generator enforces, not a note Alex has to remember to give (#57).  — Second ship: the candidate source-of-truth grew the thing the job search kept stumbling on — proof of selling technical products to technical buyers. Three roles now carry it explicitly (Meltwater's API as a data-integration sale into CRM, BI, cloud and on-prem databases and data lakes; Curalate's expansion motion of graduating clients to full custom API implementations across web, email, mobile and in-store touchpoints; Bluewolf's managed database administration and custom Salesforce consulting), plus a competency entry so every future resume and interview-prep inherits it instead of rediscovering it. The same pass hardened the ICP: a $200K OTE floor with the $200–300K band explicitly not penalized, and Mid-Market at a top-tier company scoring as a full fit on mechanism — the step-back-to-step-forward move made legible to the scanner. The value: the through-line that answers the one question standing between an account-management track record and an AI-native commercial seat now lives in the source of truth, not in a single application.

2026-09-08.headline: The job search becomes a system
2026-09-08.summary: Shipped Job-Search Engine v1 (Phase A+B, YED-146–152): repositioned role-radar from a generic scanner into a Target-Role ICP filter anchored on the me-model — the candidate source-of-truth authored days earlier — then ran it live end-to-end, 158 roles scored into the Notion Roles DB. Hardened the rubric from that real run: exemptions so good roles don't drop on a technicality (hybrid new+existing, PLG-primary, an intangibles lever), an IC-vs-people-management gate (does the role carry a personal book?), and a wider title keep-list that closes real misses (Sierra, Snorkel) — every exemption reasoned in Notes so it's auditable. Cross-provider quorum judged PASS (Sonnet 0.81 / Gemini 1.0), with 7 leadership roles JD-verified and demoted A→C in the same run. The value: the parallel job search stops being ad-hoc browsing and becomes an instrumented, ICP-scored pipeline that sharpens itself from its own output (#56).

2026-08-31.headline: Reps on the host's own stack, as the demo
2026-08-31.summary: Scaffolded Signal Stream — a real-time GTM signal agent built on Confluent's own stack (Kafka + Flink ML_PREDICT + managed MCP + RAG) — as warm-up for Confluent AI Day NYC, so the prep doubles as reps on the event's stack and a working opener for the Confluent-for-Startups lead. Built in three independently-demoable layers: query a live topic in natural language → classify each stream event against the ICP into Notion → a stretch multi-agent situation room; stdlib-only, with the producer and sink tested against live data. Deliberately scaffold-only, with the fast-moving Flink AI SQL flagged in-file as needs-verifying rather than claimed working — honest about what compiles versus what's proven. The value: it turns event attendance into a demo on the room's own terms — the documentarian edge applied to a hackathon (#55). The Confluent AI Day carousel shipped alongside.

2026-08-28.headline: Co-creation gets a real gate, and the content finally gets a mirror
2026-08-28.summary: Split the pre-research steering interview into two touches (YED-143): a light, skippable Aim before the research fan-out, and a Sharpen gate after the brief that puts ≤3 genuine forks — derived from what the prep actually surfaced — to Alex before drafting. The insight: real co-creation comes from informed forks that only exist after the research ("the transcript leaned on X but your angle says Y — which post?"), not generic up-front prompts, so the fix was to split the intake, not move it; wired to auto-fire across five content flows.  — Second ship (hub): the Content Performance dashboard, a point-in-time read of 50 LinkedIn posts answering the question under the whole post-performance thread — who does the content actually reach? It surfaced the topic→audience finding (GTM posts reach founders+GTM 54%, technical posts reach engineers 65%), visuals out-engaging text ~2.4×, and a reach≠resonance gap — and cleared the repo's pre-existing lint so the hub build goes green again. The value: the pipeline now co-creates by construction, and Alex can finally see whether the audience he's reaching is the one he's targeting (#54, hub #13).

2026-08-25.headline: The gate that can't close green on a thin brief
2026-08-25.summary: Turned the Deep Read from a step you could silently skip into one the run fails without. A local ledger marks each event pending at commit and rendered only on success; a fail-closed Stop hook plus an in-conversation marker re-check then fail any run that closes with an unrendered Deep Read — and, most importantly, write it to a durable failure log so a thin brief can't stay invisible the way 38 of them did on Aug 24. The prior fix (YED-138) was prose discipline an agent can skip; this is mechanical. Adversarially reviewed (four real false-green/invisibility holes found and fixed), quorum-judged PASS, DoD closed, with the residual-hardening edges logged as a follow-up rather than overclaimed.  — Second ship: a pronoun-fidelity rule in the brief renderer — never infer a person's pronouns from their name, default they/them until a source confirms — after it silently misgendered a real speaker from their name. Small rule, but it stops a real person being mislabeled in content Alex may tag them in; the parallel name-fidelity fix also got its long-pending validation cleared in the same render.

2026-08-21.headline: A better brief and a truer voice
2026-08-21.summary: Wired the research brief v2: one artifact with a phone-glanceable Scan head in the room, and a deep, cited, novice-friendly prose “commute read” rendered afterward and appended without ever blocking the pipeline. The old output had regressed to a machine-readable bullet lattice; this restores flowing analysis and adds a historical spine, inline-defined jargon, and end-to-end source citations. The value is a briefing worth reading on the train that walks Alex into a room genuinely conversant — and a richer substrate every downstream post draws from.  — Second ship of the day: the audience-first ethos went from charter to production (YED-103). The north-star document existed but no content skill actually read it, so posts kept drifting back to self-as-protagonist; this wired it into the six content surfaces and codified the “ordering, not erasure” counterweight (so “decenter yourself” stops collapsing into self-erasure that reads junior to a buyer), the three floors, a softened voice rule, and a mandatory 3–5 “learn more” citation set on every post. The value: the pipeline now generates audience-first content by construction, not just on paper — shipped, judged pass cross-provider, DoD closed.  — Third ship: the brief-v2 wiring finally got its live end-to-end acceptance test, which last session's frozen agent registry made impossible. Ran the whole pipeline on a real event (Elastic NYC × Plural) — four specialists, synthesizer, five Notion writes, then the Deep Read rendered section-by-section on Opus and appended decoupled. The render cleared the Daytona spike bar and closed its one open gap: endnotes now carry real source URLs end to end (specialist ledger → synthesizer evidence set → renderer), quorum-judged PASS (Sonnet 0.896 / Gemini 1.0). It also caught a genuine renderer bug — confabulated speaker first names in the sections where the speakers were only passing references — corrected in-run and then hardened out of the spec so the standing pipeline reproduces names verbatim. Decoupling held: the Scan head and every entity record committed independently of the render. The value: brief-v2 is proven in production rather than merely wired, with the one real defect found and fixed before merge (#47).

2026-08-07.headline: The portfolio starts maintaining itself
2026-08-07.summary: Shipped the self-instrumenting build journal — a generator that assembles each build day's facts from git and telemetry, a human-owned prose sidecar, a /journal page on the hub, and a Stop hook that regenerates it automatically. Also restructured the build arcs into foundation-anchored themes and made one canonical JSON the single source for both the hub page and the shareable artifact. The portfolio now documents itself, and two surfaces can no longer drift apart.

2026-08-06.headline: The build-arcs surface + the first live intelligence run
2026-08-06.summary: Shipped the public Build Arcs page (3 → 13 arcs, themed) and a shareable artifact, so a month of work is legible to a hiring manager at a glance. Ran the progressive market-intelligence engine live for the first time — seven cited signals, a new topic, a recomputed viewpoint — entirely on subscription, zero API tokens. The portfolio now shows an instrumented system that documents and re-ranks itself, not just claims it does.

2026-08-05.headline: Branch-first discipline, promoted to canonical
2026-08-05.summary: Landed the governed batch: branch-first git discipline and a hook-schema reference, promoted into the cross-project canonical config, plus the hub's build-in-public content (changelog + candid README). Enforced in a hook rather than left to habit, so the right change-management path is the default in every project, not a thing to remember. Makes disciplined, reviewable change the paved road.

2026-07-31.headline: Promoting the proven primitives
2026-07-31.summary: Swept the strongest Empire State primitives — the toolbox skill, the PostHog/Vercel and hook-schema references — into the personal plugin via governed PRs, and added a toolbox/counts generator so the build-in-public surface can't drift from reality. Validate locally, promote deliberately. Every future project now inherits accumulated discipline automatically.

2026-07-30.headline: A dedicated telemetry project
2026-07-30.summary: Repointed build-rigor telemetry to its own PostHog project so build signal isn't mixed with product analytics, with read and write keys split by scope. Observability for the delivery system deserves the same rigor as the product. Clean, trustworthy build telemetry the hub can read honestly.

2026-07-21.headline: The cross-provider judge
2026-07-21.summary: Wired a second, cross-provider judge (Gemini alongside Sonnet) into the build-quality gate and mechanized the dangling-reference check. An LLM grading its own model family self-prefers; a different provider is the cheapest robust mitigation. Build quality now gets an independent, adversarial second opinion instead of a rubber stamp.

2026-07-17.headline: Closing the rigor loop + judge calibration
2026-07-17.summary: Calibrated the judge against a human anchor — crossing the trust gate to provisional-trusted — and wired the missing writer so DoD telemetry fields stop coming back null. Rigor that isn't written to the execution path decays silently. Rigor became measurable where the work actually happens, not in an optional doc.

2026-07-15.headline: The command-orchestration convention
2026-07-15.summary: Authored the required command skeleton (intake → dispatch → collect → synthesize → named output) after a thin, declarative command failed the quality bar, and ran live LLM-as-judge execution. A command that only lists agents without dispatch/output logic isn't done. Commands now meet a completeness standard the judge can enforce.

2026-07-11.headline: Rigor loop close + drift cleanup
2026-07-11.summary: Closed the first pass of the rigor loop and fixed confirmed documentation drift across the project config. Source-of-truth docs that lie are worse than none. The running system and its documentation agree again.
